repository_role: Cross-program development lane only; not part of the active FCP New Phytologist manuscript.
central_question: Do the same biological properties predict how rapidly phenotypic and interaction information is lost across evolutionary time and geographic space?

conceptual_units.panel: A lineage-defined set of focal species analyzed under one response domain and one source contract.
conceptual_units.focal_species: A species contributing spatially replicated observations within a panel.
conceptual_units.local_network: An observed site/time interaction network, not a predicted metaweb.

response_axes.name: trait temporal memory loss
response_axes.distance_axis: phylogenetic distance among focal species within a panel
response_axes.state: same homologous trait variable measured at species level
response_axes.response: trait dissimilarity above a frequency/measurement null as phylogenetic distance increases
response_axes.sign_convention: larger positive lambda = faster temporal loss / lability

response_axes.name: trait spatial turnover
response_axes.distance_axis: geographic distance among observations/sites within focal species
response_axes.state: the same trait variable used in T_TRAIT
response_axes.response: within-species trait dissimilarity as geographic distance increases
response_axes.primary_summary: median lambda_trait_space across eligible focal species
response_axes.sign_convention: larger positive lambda = faster spatial turnover

response_axes.name: interaction temporal memory loss
response_axes.distance_axis: phylogenetic distance among focal species within a panel
response_axes.state: observed interaction-partner profile after partner taxonomy harmonization
response_axes.response: partner-profile dissimilarity as focal-species phylogenetic distance increases
response_axes.sign_convention: larger positive lambda = faster loss of partner identity across evolution

response_axes.name: interaction spatial rewiring
response_axes.distance_axis: geographic distance among local networks for the same focal species
response_axes.response: partner-profile turnover among sites, decomposed into partner availability turnover and rewiring among co-occurring partners
response_axes.primary_summary: median lambda_interaction_space_rewiring across eligible focal species
response_axes.sign_convention: larger positive lambda = faster geographic rewiring

primary_predictor_families.definition: Within-panel heterogeneity in the abiotic and biotic contexts experienced by focal taxa, computed without using any turnover response.

operationalization.trait_arm: environmental heterogeneity across georeferenced trait observations/ranges
operationalization.interaction_arm: partner-community opportunity heterogeneity across local networks

primary_predictor_families.frozen_direction: higher heterogeneity -> faster temporal and faster spatial turnover

primary_predictor_families.definition: Narrowness of ecological or partner use, standardized within taxonomic/source panel before cross-panel synthesis.

operationalization.trait_arm: habitat/resource niche breadth from independent occurrence/trait metadata
operationalization.interaction_arm: effective partner breadth from an observation-effort-corrected partner profile

primary_predictor_families.frozen_direction: specialization may strengthen temporal retention while increasing local sensitivity to partner replacement; opposite axis effects are allowed and are the prediction.

primary_predictor_families.definition: Taxon-appropriate movement/dispersal capacity from an external trait source, standardized within major taxonomic group.

examples: bird hand-wing index or migration strategy
plant dispersal syndrome or seed-mass-linked dispersal proxy only if frozen before response opening

primary_predictor_families.frozen_direction: higher mobility should reduce geographic turnover more strongly than evolutionary turnover.

primary_tests.test: Across eligible lineage panels, Spearman(lambda_trait_time, lambda_trait_space)
primary_tests.interpretation: Do phenotypically labile lineages in evolutionary time also turn over rapidly across geographic space?

primary_tests.test: Across eligible lineage panels, Spearman(lambda_interaction_time, lambda_interaction_space_rewiring)
primary_tests.interpretation: Do lineages that rapidly change interaction partners across evolution also rewire rapidly across geography?

primary_tests.test: Multivariate/hierarchical comparison of predictor coefficients across the four response axes
primary_tests.interpretation: Which biological properties are common couplers and which systematically decouple time from space?

primary_tests.test: Only in panels with all four responses: compare trait and interaction turnover signatures without treating missing cells as zero.
primary_tests.interpretation: Does phenotypic lability covary with interaction lability within the same biological lineages?

null_and_bias_rules.trait_space: Permute complete trait observations among observed coordinates within focal species while preserving sampling geometry and measurement rows.
null_and_bias_rules.interaction_time: Condition on focal and partner marginal observation opportunity; partner richness alone may not create phylogenetic memory.
null_and_bias_rules.interaction_space: Partition total network beta diversity into species/partner turnover and rewiring; the primary S_INT response is rewiring conditional on co-occurrence/opportunity, not raw network dissimilarity.
null_and_bias_rules.source_effort: No interaction database record count is interpreted as preference without a source-specific effort model or bounded binary-presence estimand.
null_and_bias_rules.taxonomy: No post-outcome synonym expansion or taxonomic broadening.
null_and_bias_rules.missingness: A missing response cell is NOT_EVALUABLE, never zero.

trait_arm.evidence: ~91,970 measurements, 978 vascular plant species, >99% georeferenced, mostly individual-level

trait_arm.source: AVONET + spatially repeated bird trait source

interaction_arm.evidence: ecological interaction network database with network-level metadata

interaction_arm.role: broad spatial-temporal interaction source and transport candidate
interaction_arm.evidence: spatial-temporal species interaction records searchable by location, interaction type and taxon

eligibility_sequence: panel construction without biological turnover responses
minimum coverage for both time and space within an arm

relation_to_existing_projects.CHUN: proof of concept for evolutionary-time phenotype memory; not an input response unless used only in a later declared transport analysis
relation_to_existing_projects.FCP: proof of concept for geographic phenotype organization and reusable spatial estimators; active paper science remains unchanged
relation_to_existing_projects.IWE: interaction-timing meta-analysis; conceptually relevant but not counted as a turnover replicate
relation_to_existing_projects.TTF: qualification/abstention methodology can be reused, but this programme is biological rather than a TTF methods paper

primary_trait_family.selection_basis: Coverage + biological complementarity, frozen before any temporal/spatial turnover coefficient is computed.
traits: Leaf area per leaf dry mass (specific leaf area, SLA)
Leaf dry mass per leaf fresh mass (Leaf dry matter content, LDMC)
Leaf nitrogen (N) content per leaf dry mass
primary_trait_family.rationale: Four complementary axes: acquisitive leaf economics, tissue dry-matter strategy, stature, and nutrient economics. All passed the paired source coverage gate.

mangal_interaction_type_admission.rule: For each Mangal interaction type and directed role (from/to), retain as a candidate only if >=20 reference taxa each occur in >=3 georeferenced networks. Rank by repeated-taxon count, then network count, then lexical type/role; admit at most 3 candidate type-role families before any partner-turnover statistic is computed.
